Branch `claude/project-prompt-harness` (worktree `.claude/worktrees/project-prompt-harness`), commit 70366449ae on jusprin-newui 336facf825. Not pushed. Baseline run 2026-10-15 at Kenneth's request (29df4b87f8): today's prompt 6b4b8b6188, 3 runs: 39/54 pass, 4 fail, 11 unobserved; 599,356 input tokens (459,776 cached), 9,784 output, 3 judge calls. The model often reads before replying, so first-person and reply-in-german observed no reply (0 pass, 3 unobserved each); answer-from-context 0/3 (calls workspace_inspect).

Design that differs from the 2026-10-15 handover, and why:
- Requests are recorded whole by a new shell harness mode, `--project-prompt-requests <script.json> <out.json>`: the project chat's real OpenAIResponsesAgent with a transport that holds each request; the scenario answers with scripted model outputs, so tools run for real and the app builds every request. `--manual-mcp` could not do it: in-turn tool results carry a `workspace` block (AgentHost::continue_after_tool, `context_json`) that MCP results never contain, and MCP rewrites stale errors to `stale_workspace` (in-app also says `stale_workspace` now).
- Case 16 uses the printer start G-code (22 KB) because presets_list pages at 25 (~1.5 KB) and every other read here stays under 4 KB: the 16 KiB omission note never fires for them.
- Cases 7/8 use initial_layer_print_height 0.5: a hand-typed layer_height above max_layer_height (0.28) is reset by an Orca dialog.
- Case 18's 3MF is written by the recorder (model_info->description + export_3mf); a PrusaSlicer 3MF loads geometry only and drops the description.

App problems found while recording (reported, not fixed): printer_setup_preview says valid/no mismatch for Bambu PETG HF on Smooth Cool Plate, then Orca refuses to slice; slice_start wait:true on that plate stays running (up to 15 min by the code) instead of failing.

**Why:** the next session runs Kenneth's batch or re-records after tool changes.
**How to apply:** re-record with the harness command in tests/project_prompt/README.md after tool/result changes; batch needs Kenneth's approval and the rewritten prompt. Related: [[project-prompt-harness-critique]], [[prompt-eval-spend-budget]], [[manual-mcp-tool-repro-recipe]].

**2026-10-15 later: Kenneth reversed the strict one-step rule for reads** (a9ffaf06e6): a read the case doesn't decide on is answered from real results the recorder captured at that point (workspace_inspect, slice_report, printer_list, settings_get of 32 keys for print + first object), max 3 per run; changes/judged calls still end the run. He wants flexibility, not exact-path expectations ("LMs are not deterministic"). First single run: 7 of 23 ended "no recorded answer" (settings_search, filament keys, legacy keys like fill_density, object_analyze, string targets) — answer coverage is the open weakness.

**Baseline with answered reads (f911bad664, 2026-10-15):** 23 cases x 3 on 6b4b8b6188, recording 80eddcbe9e (27 answers/point, requests.json ~4 MB): 47/69 pass, 8 fail, 14 unobserved; 1,256,920 input tokens (925,696 cached). Unobserved = string-JSON targets (app refuses), free-worded settings_search, object_analyze, unrecorded keys. Older 39/54 baseline not comparable.

**346a811aad (2026-10-15):** recording adds object_analyze per active-plate object (eachObject), 49 word-order-free settings_search queries, a few more names; workspace block stored once per point (sharedWorkspace) and reinserted byte-exact by the runner. requests.json ~6.7 MB (searches ~4.3 MB). 10 of the baseline's 14 unanswered reads now covered (offline replay); the 4 left are string-JSON targets. Not yet run live on this recording.

**708735c9ab:** reran the 7 cases with unanswered reads on 346a811aad (21 runs, 602,761 input tokens); baseline now 52/69 pass, 10 fail, 7 unobserved (rows marked by recording). Remaining misses: single setting names (slow_down_layers, bridge_no_support, filament_ramming_parameters), search wordings, string targets. Commit message wrongly says "13 of 21 passed, 6 unobserved"; correct is 12 passed, 7 unobserved (README is right).

**c3f858480b:** recorder reads every setting per scope (keys from empty-query settings_search) plus wrong-scope names; settingItems table, requests.json 3.2 MB; 22 of 29 earlier unanswered reads now covered; rest are string targets, changedOnly searches, unrecorded search wordings.

**Squashed 2026-10-15 at Kenneth's request:** all branch commits are now one, 4072f22e84 on 336facf825 (tree identical to the last pre-squash commit); every hash above except 336facf825/6b4b8b6188 no longer exists. Final baseline 52/69 pass, 10 fail, 7 unobserved; README names recordings 1/2/3 instead of hashes. Not pushed.

**Merged 2026-10-15:** rebased onto Kenneth's two local commits (6c68b5489f, f3c5defb71) and fast-forwarded local jusprin-newui to 5ae439525b; tests passed after rebase. Not pushed: local jusprin-newui is 3 ahead of origin, 2 of them Kenneth's.

name: never-reuse-another-sessions-worktree
description: "A clean, merged, idle worktree under .claude/worktrees still belongs to its session; its owner can resume and check out over you mid-run. Always create your own."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: cb4c8804-b0a0-4ca0-b4a5-6b6998947d4b
  modified: 2026-09-24T00:36:34.672Z
---

On 2026-09-23 I reused `.claude/worktrees/compassionate-gould-f98259` to skip a full build: it was clean, detached at a commit already merged into jusprin-newui, no process had files open there, and its build dir was only 9 days old. An hour later its owning session resumed, checked out two other branches there (the reflog shows it), rewrote ~13,800 resource files, and my running harness crashed with "Could not load bitmap: bed_high_templ" -- a symptom that looked like a product bug.

**Why:** "clean and idle" says nothing about ownership. The session that created a worktree can resume at any time, and it has no way to know someone else moved in.

**How to apply:** create a new worktree with its own name (`git worktree add -b <branch> .claude/worktrees/<name> <base>`) and configure a fresh build dir with the flags in [[jusprin-worktree-build]]. At jusprin-newui bd8ea51abc a fresh build of `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs agent_bridge_tests shell_integration_harness` was 881 ninja steps, not the hour I feared. If a harness run dies strangely, check `git -C <worktree> reflog -3 --date=iso` and file mtimes before suspecting the code. Related: [[subagent-worktrees-create-manually]].

name: printer-setup-bed-type-check
description: "2026-10-15: agent previews and mutations never run Orca's slice-time Print::validate, so 5 of 6 tried changes were called fine and then refused at slicing; Kenneth said no one-off fix, find the pattern; awaiting direction."
metadata:
  type: project
---

Reproduced 2026-10-15 in worktree distracted-lehmann-9c1b12, branch `claude/bed-type-mismatch` at jusprin-newui 336facf825 (no code changes). On the `--manual-mcp` fixture (X1C 0.4, Smooth Cool Plate), `printer_setup_preview {"filamentPresets": ["Bambu PETG HF @BBL X1C"]}` returns valid, no issues, no mismatches; `printer_setup` applies it; Orca's log then says "Plate 1: Cool Plate is not suggested for use printing filament 1 (Bambu PETG HF)...". Raising the filament's `cool_plate_temp` and `cool_plate_temp_initial_layer` to 60 with settings_apply_patch makes both plates slice.

Orca's rule (Print::validate, Print.cpp ~1754): on a Bambu printer or one with `support_multi_bed_types`, any filament used by an object whose `get_bed_temp_key(curr_bed_type)` value is 0 blocks slicing. Orca lets a person select the pair; it refuses only at validation.

`mismatches` in the preview means configured vs observed (device or user-confirmed fact); a plate/filament conflict has no observed side. `issues` make `valid: false`, which also makes `printer_setup` refuse at submit (ToolExecutionCoordinator ~670), stricter than Orca.

First proposal (one-off warning) was rejected by Kenneth: "We can't change code just to fix this problem"; he asked for the pattern. Widened search, same day, same fixture: settings_preview_patch filament cool_plate_temp 0, process initial_layer_print_height 0.5 (> 0.4 nozzle; project_prompt cases 7/8 use this value), spiral_mode with two copies on a plate; plate_layout bedType Engineering Plate with PLA (no preview); object_place scaleTo z 300 (no preview, model_fits 0). All accepted, all refused at slicing. plate_layout extruder 2 was refused up front (a copied check exists). Pattern: previews copy Orca checks piece by piece (dialogs + config-only Slic3r::validate), never Print::validate (~35 blocking rules); and after any change the agent hears nothing: slice_start started:true, slice_report valid:false with no reason; only an issue notice's Resolve/Ask AI hands Orca's message to the agent. PrintIssueMonitor already runs Print::validate on the live state. Old one-off idea, kept for reference: a non-blocking warning, following the skipped_confirmation precedent ([[orca-edit-questions-forwarded]]). Waiting on his choice. If the tool output schema changes, re-record tests/project_prompt/requests.json ([[project-prompt-harness-ported]]).

name: prompt-eval-spend-budget
description: No live-model prompt tests without Kenneth approving a specific batch; my stub run-to-the-end design burned 300M+ tokens and the OpenRouter monthly limit (2026-10-10).
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

On 2026-10-08 to 10 my live prompt tests used more than 300M tokens on the OpenRouter key (`~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env`) and hit its monthly limit. Kenneth's verdict on 2026-10-10: letting the agent wander on stub replies for 16 requests was a stupid design. I agree.

What went wrong, specifically:
- Every request carries about 10k input tokens (prompt plus 29 tool definitions); with `store:false` every tool call resends all of it plus the history.
- About 1,300 runs were "stub tools, run to the end": I removed the stop line from `tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py`'s loop and let conversations continue to a 16-request cap on its canned replies (`workspace_result`: six tools get a fixed answer, the rest `{"accepted": true}`). The replies never answer the model's question, so it wandered 10–19 calls; about 150–200k tokens per run, 195–260M in total. The simulator runs (about 630, about 40M) and first-step runs (about 500, about 12M) were the cheap part.
- It began as a one-off shortcut, I kept it "for comparability", then chased its noise with more runs. The scripts logged no usage.

**Why:** the money, and the numbers were also bad: most unrequested slices came after about 15 empty reads, so the test partly provoked what it counted.

**How to apply (Kenneth's instructions, 2026-10-10):**
- Run no live-model tests until Kenneth approves a specific batch. A `403 Key limit exceeded` means stop; do not switch keys or route around it.
- Never run conversations to the end on canned tool replies. Use the stateful simulator (`run_workflow_tests.py`, `workflow_fixture.py`) and the committed first-step test (stops at the first tool call, 8-request cap). If more varied full conversations are needed, extend the simulator so replies answer what was asked.
- Before a batch: state runs × tokens (about 65k per simulator run, about 25k per first-step run), one control, one round. Log `usage` from every response and report the actual total.
- Keep stub-derived rates out of the repo and out of reports.

Related: [[project-prompt-eval-sample-size]].

On 2026-09-23 I reused `.claude/worktrees/compassionate-gould-f98259` to skip a full build: it was clean, detached at a commit already merged into jusprin-newui, no process had files open there, and its build dir was only 9 days old. name: printer-setup-bed-type-check
description: "2026-10-15: agent previews and mutations never run Orca's slice-time Print::validate, so 5 of 6 tried changes were called fine and then refused at slicing; Kenneth said no one-off fix, find the pattern; awaiting direction."
metadata:
  type: project
---

Reproduced 2026-10-15 in worktree distracted-lehmann-9c1b12, branch `claude/bed-type-mismatch` at jusprin-newui 336facf825 (no code changes). On the `--manual-mcp` fixture (X1C 0.4, Smooth Cool Plate), `printer_setup_preview {"filamentPresets": ["Bambu PETG HF @BBL X1C"]}` returns valid, no issues, no mismatches; `printer_setup` applies it; Orca's log then says "Plate 1: Cool Plate is not suggested for use printing filament 1 (Bambu PETG HF)...". Raising the filament's `cool_plate_temp` and `cool_plate_temp_initial_layer` to 60 with settings_apply_patch makes both plates slice.

Orca's rule (Print::validate, Print.cpp ~1754): on a Bambu printer or one with `support_multi_bed_types`, any filament used by an object whose `get_bed_temp_key(curr_bed_type)` value is 0 blocks slicing. Orca lets a person select the pair; it refuses only at validation.

`mismatches` in the preview means configured vs observed (device or user-confirmed fact); a plate/filament conflict has no observed side. `issues` make `valid: false`, which also makes `printer_setup` refuse at submit (ToolExecutionCoordinator ~670), stricter than Orca.

First proposal (one-off warning) was rejected by Kenneth: "We can't change code just to fix this problem"; he asked for the pattern. Widened search, same day, same fixture: settings_preview_patch filament cool_plate_temp 0, process initial_layer_print_height 0.5 (> 0.4 nozzle; project_prompt cases 7/8 use this value), spiral_mode with two copies on a plate; plate_layout bedType Engineering Plate with PLA (no preview); object_place scaleTo z 300 (no preview, model_fits 0). All accepted, all refused at slicing. plate_layout extruder 2 was refused up front (a copied check exists). Pattern: previews copy Orca checks piece by piece (dialogs + config-only Slic3r::validate), never Print::validate (~35 blocking rules); and after any change the agent hears nothing: slice_start started:true, slice_report valid:false with no reason; only an issue notice's Resolve/Ask AI hands Orca's message to the agent. PrintIssueMonitor already runs Print::validate on the live state. Old one-off idea, kept for reference: a non-blocking warning, following the skipped_confirmation precedent ([[orca-edit-questions-forwarded]]). Waiting on his choice. If the tool output schema changes, re-record tests/project_prompt/requests.json ([[project-prompt-harness-ported]]).

name: prompt-eval-spend-budget
description: No live-model prompt tests without Kenneth approving a specific batch; my stub run-to-the-end design burned 300M+ tokens and the OpenRouter monthly limit (2026-10-10).
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

On 2026-10-08 to 10 my live prompt tests used more than 300M tokens on the OpenRouter key (`~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env`) and hit its monthly limit. Kenneth's verdict on 2026-10-10: letting the agent wander on stub replies for 16 requests was a stupid design. I agree.

What went wrong, specifically:
- Every request carries about 10k input tokens (prompt plus 29 tool definitions); with `store:false` every tool call resends all of it plus the history.
- About 1,300 runs were "stub tools, run to the end": I removed the stop line from `tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py`'s loop and let conversations continue to a 16-request cap on its canned replies (`workspace_result`: six tools get a fixed answer, the rest `{"accepted": true}`). The replies never answer the model's question, so it wandered 10–19 calls; about 150–200k tokens per run, 195–260M in total. The simulator runs (about 630, about 40M) and first-step runs (about 500, about 12M) were the cheap part.
- It began as a one-off shortcut, I kept it "for comparability", then chased its noise with more runs. The scripts logged no usage.

**Why:** the money, and the numbers were also bad: most unrequested slices came after about 15 empty reads, so the test partly provoked what it counted.

**How to apply (Kenneth's instructions, 2026-10-10):**
- Run no live-model tests until Kenneth approves a specific batch. A `403 Key limit exceeded` means stop; do not switch keys or route around it.
- Never run conversations to the end on canned tool replies. Use the stateful simulator (`run_workflow_tests.py`, `workflow_fixture.py`) and the committed first-step test (stops at the first tool call, 8-request cap). If more varied full conversations are needed, extend the simulator so replies answer what was asked.
- Before a batch: state runs × tokens (about 65k per simulator run, about 25k per first-step run), one control, one round. Log `usage` from every response and report the actual total.
- Keep stub-derived rates out of the repo and out of reports.

Related: [[project-prompt-eval-sample-size]].

"""Adds the cases of a recording made from part of script.json to
requests.json, leaving every case already there byte for byte, and keeping
each distinct setting item once file-wide, as the recorder does."""
import json
import sys

target_path, new_path = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
target = json.load(open(target_path, encoding="utf-8"))
new = json.load(open(new_path, encoding="utf-8"))
key = lambda item: json.dumps(item, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False)
index = {key(item): i for i, item in enumerate(target["settingItems"])}
added = 0
for name, case in new["cases"].items():
    assert name not in target["cases"], name
    for answer in case["answers"]:
        if not answer.get("settingItems"):
            continue
        output = json.loads(answer["output"])
        for field in ("items", "unknownKeys"):
            if field not in output["result"]:
                continue
            remapped = []
            for i in output["result"][field]:
                item = new["settingItems"][i]
                k = key(item)
                if k not in index:
                    index[k] = len(target["settingItems"])
                    target["settingItems"].append(item)
                    added += 1
                remapped.append(index[k])
            output["result"][field] = remapped
        # nlohmann writes the output string compact with sorted keys
        answer["output"] = json.dumps(output, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False)
    target["cases"][name] = case
target["cases"] = dict(sorted(target["cases"].items()))
open(target_path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(json.dumps(target, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
print(f"added {len(new['cases'])} cases, {added} new setting items", file=sys.stderr)

new = json.load(open(new_path, encoding="utf-8"))

    for answer in case["answers"]:
        if not answer.get("settingItems"):
            continue
        output = json.loads(answer["output"])
        for field in ("items", "unknownKeys"):
            if field not in output["result"]:
                continue
            remapped = []
            for i in output["result"][field]:
                item = new["settingItems"][i]
                k = key(item)
                if k not in index:
                    index[k] = len(target["settingItems"])
                    target["settingItems"].append(item)
                    added += 1

    target["cases"][name] = case

git add tests/data/jusprin/harness.conf tests/project_prompt tests/shell/project_prompt_scenario.inc && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Add two project prompt cases about asking before printing

The project prompt tests had no case for the When-to-act sentence that asks
the assistant to ask what an object is for, and none for reassessing a setup
after the material changes. Live conversations on 2026-10-15 found the app
failing both: once in three it sliced at once on "I want to print this", and
after a switch to Bambu PETG HF it never noticed the project's Cool Plate,
on which OrcaSlicer refuses to slice that filament.

print-this-no-purpose sends "I want to print this" with nothing said about
the purpose. It passes on a reply that asks exactly one question the person
must answer (judged), and fails on any change, slice_start or an
intent_update included. petg-on-cool-plate holds a printer_setup_preview and
printer_setup to Bambu PETG HF on the Smooth Cool Plate, both valid, then
"ok, print it". It passes on printer_setup_preview or a reply that raises the
plate (judged), and fails on slice_start or a reply that does not.

Both points were recorded from the app and added to requests.json without
touching the 23 recorded points. Three recorder changes made that possible:

- A conversation in script.json can name a plateType that the person selects
  before the fixture's slice. Without it every conversation after "prepare"
  starts on the Textured PEI Plate that conversation selected.
- The recorder waits for OrcaSlicer's scheduled update before each new
  message. Without it, the message after the filament switch reported the
  plate as still sliced with a current estimate, which OrcaSlicer marks stale
  a few seconds later. A full re-record shows no earlier point changes.
- The harness config points OrcaSlicer's update check at a closed port. The
  version server now reports v2.5.0-alpha, newer than this build, and the
  update prompt it opened stalled the recorder.

The default run budget goes from 69 to 75 so every case still runs three
times. The README lists both cases and their first three runs each: 0 of 3
passed in both. The first case's runs asked a second question about which of
the fixture's two plates to print; no run sliced. No PETG run raised the
plate.
EOF

Add two project prompt cases about asking before printing

The project prompt tests had no case for the When-to-act sentence that asks
the assistant to ask what an object is for, and none for reassessing a setup
after the material changes. Live conversations on 2026-10-15 found the app
failing both: once in three it sliced at once on "I want to print this", and
after a switch to Bambu PETG HF it never noticed the project's Cool Plate,
on which OrcaSlicer refuses to slice that filament.

print-this-no-purpose sends "I want to print this" with nothing said about
the purpose. It passes on a reply that asks exactly one question the person
must answer (judged), and fails on any change, slice_start or an
intent_update included. petg-on-cool-plate holds a printer_setup_preview and
printer_setup to Bambu PETG HF on the Smooth Cool Plate, both valid, then
"ok, print it". It passes on printer_setup_preview or a reply that raises the
plate (judged), and fails on slice_start or a reply that does not.

Both points were recorded from the app and added to requests.json without
touching the 23 recorded points. Three recorder changes made that possible:

- A conversation in script.json can name a plateType that the person selects
  before the fixture's slice. Without it every conversation after "prepare"
  starts on the Textured PEI Plate that conversation selected.
- The recorder waits for OrcaSlicer's scheduled update before each new
  message. Without it, the message after the filament switch reported the
  plate as still sliced with a current estimate, which OrcaSlicer marks stale
  a few seconds later. A full re-record shows no earlier point changes.
- The harness config points OrcaSlicer's update check at a closed port. The
  version server now reports v2.5.0-alpha, newer than this build, and the
  update prompt it opened stalled the recorder.

The default run budget goes from 69 to 75 so every case still runs three
times. The README lists both cases and their first three runs each: 0 of 3
passed in both. The first case's runs asked a second question about which of
the fixture's two plates to print; no run sliced. No PETG run raised the
plate.
EOF

# Two project prompt cases about asking before printing

Branch `claude/print-setup-cases`, commit f5c2cd8387 on local `jusprin-newui` 36d33312ed (the squash of 7607c8fe42). Not pushed. The plate-type task (task_cf88936b) had not landed, so the workspace block in these recordings does not carry the plate type.

## The problem

Live conversations on 2026-10-15 showed two faults the project prompt tests in `tests/project_prompt` could not see. Once in three, "I want to print this" sliced the existing PLA setup at once instead of asking what the part is for. And after a switch to Bambu PETG HF, the assistant never noticed the project's Cool Plate, on which OrcaSlicer refuses to slice that filament.

## What I added

`print-this-no-purpose` sends "I want to print this" to the usual two-plate fixture, PLA on the Smooth Cool Plate, plate 1 sliced. It passes when the judge reads the reply as asking exactly one question the person must answer, and fails on any change or on a reply that does not. It tests "Ask when the answer is theirs… what the object is for".

`petg-on-cool-plate` has a history in which the person asked for Bambu PETG HF and the assistant ran `printer_setup_preview` and `printer_setup`, both valid on the Smooth Cool Plate, then "ok, print it". It passes on `printer_setup_preview`, or on a reply that raises the plate (judged). It fails on `slice_start`, and also on a reply that ignores the plate; the brief listed only `slice_start`, and I added the second because that reply is the fault itself. Another change is unobserved. It tests "Reassess when the purpose, material, printer or an object changes."

Recording needed three harness fixes. Without them the recording would have been wrong or would not have run at all. First, every conversation after `prepare` inherited its Textured PEI Plate, so a conversation can now name a `plateType` that the person selects before the fixture's slice. Second, the recorder sent "ok, print it" before OrcaSlicer had processed the filament switch, so the message claimed plate 1 was still sliced; it now waits for OrcaSlicer's scheduled update first. Third, OrcaSlicer's version server now reports v2.5.0-alpha, and its update prompt froze the harness; the harness config now points the check at a closed port. A full re-record matched all 23 existing points apart from ids, timestamps and temporary paths, and those points are unchanged byte for byte in `requests.json`.

## Tests and results

`--render-only` works for both cases and for the whole suite (25 cases × 3). The `[project]` native tests passed: the tool list has not drifted, and every recorded result, new ones included, matches its schema.

Three live runs each on DeepSeek V4 Flash: 13 requests, 143,784 input tokens (80,896 cached), 3,664 output, plus 4 judge calls. There were no 403 errors.

`print-this-no-purpose` passed 0 of 3, failed 3. Every run read the workspace and then asked two questions: what the box is for, and which of the two plates to print. No run sliced or changed anything. The second question comes from the fixture: two plates, with the selection on the plate that is not active.

`petg-on-cool-plate` passed 0 of 3, failed 1, and 2 were unobserved. One run recorded a purpose it made up ("Test/calibration cube") and said it would slice. One asked what the box is for without mentioning the plate. One read temperature settings under names OrcaSlicer does not have. No run raised the plate, although the plate's name was in its history three times.

The current prompt passes neither case.

## Remaining issues

- A one-object fixture would let the first case measure its sentence without the plate question. Re-running after that needs your approval.
- The runner judges only the first tool call in a response. In one PETG run, an invented-purpose `intent_update` sat beside a read in the same response and went unjudged.
- Another session's harness (pid 1788, recording `requests.json` in a different worktree) will hit the same update prompt unless it has the config fix.

Problem: `tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py` builds a `Step` from the model's output and keeps only the FIRST `function_call` (`Step.__init__`). When a response holds several calls, the runner judges and answers only the first; the rest are appended to the history (`input += step.output + [...]`) with no `function_call_output`. Seen on 2026-10-16 in case `petg-on-cool-plate`, run 3: one response held `workspace_inspect` and `intent_update {"fields": [], "setupTitle": "Print 20mm calibration box in PETG HF"}` (a purpose the person never gave). The read was answered; the change was never judged. Any case that fails on "a change" can miss one this way, and later requests carry a call with no result.

Task: make the runner judge every call in a response. A reasonable rule is that a response containing any change is judged as that change (the first change, if several), and a response of reads only is answered with a recorded answer for each read (or ends unobserved when any read has no recorded answer), each result under its own call_id, as the app continues a turn. Read tests/project_prompt/README.md first (its "One step, with its reads answered" section) and keep its style; update that section to describe the rule. Do not change the prompt (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/projectInstructions.ts) or any case's check.

Verify with `tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py --render-only` and an offline unit check of the new Step logic on hand-written outputs (no model call). Do not run live-model tests: they need Kenneth's approval for a specific batch (case count, runs, token estimate); keys live in ~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env and must never be printed. Commit with a plain-English message.

content.text:
I added both cases, recorded them from the app, and ran each three times live. The current prompt passes neither: 0 of 3 in both cases. The work is committed as f5c2cd8387 on branch `claude/print-setup-cases` (based on `jusprin-newui` 36d33312ed) and not pushed. The plate-type task (task_cf88936b) had not landed, so the workspace block in these recordings does not include the plate type.

**What the runs did** (DeepSeek V4 Flash with the pinned judge; 13 requests, 143,784 input tokens of which 80,896 cached, 3,664 output, plus 4 judge calls; no 403):
- **`print-this-no-purpose`: 3 failed.** No run sliced or changed anything, so the slice-at-once fault did not show up in three runs. Each run read the workspace and then asked two questions: what the box is for, and which plate to print. The case requires exactly one question. The second question is a fair one on this fixture: it has two plates with a box on each, and the selected box is on the plate that is not active. A one-object fixture would test the prompt sentence without that noise.
- **`petg-on-cool-plate`: 1 failed, 2 unobserved.**
  - One run recorded a purpose the person never gave ("Test/calibration cube") and said it would slice. I count any change other than `slice_start` as unobserved, so this run counts as unobserved.
  - One run asked what the box is for and never mentioned the plate. That counts as a fail. You listed only `slice_start` as a fail; I also fail a reply that ignores the plate, because that reply is the fault itself.
  - One run asked for filament settings under names OrcaSlicer doesn't have, which the recording can't answer, so it is unobserved.
  - No run raised the plate, even though "Smooth Cool Plate" appears three times in the history.

**The recorder needed three fixes before the cases were usable:**
- **The plate carried over between conversations.** Every conversation after `prepare` started on the Textured PEI Plate that `prepare` selected. A conversation in `script.json` can now set `"plateType"`, and both new ones set the Cool Plate.
- **The message was sent too early.** "ok, print it" went out before OrcaSlicer had processed the filament switch, so it told the model plate 1 was still sliced. OrcaSlicer marks the slice out of date a few seconds later. The recorder now waits for that before each message.
- **Every harness run froze on an update prompt.** OrcaSlicer's version server now reports v2.5.0-alpha, newer than this 2.4.2 build, so every run opened an update dialog and stalled. The harness config now sends that check to a closed port. Until this commit reaches `jusprin-newui`, harness runs on other branches will stall the same way.

**Verification:**
- `--render-only` works for both new cases and the whole suite (25 cases, 3 runs each). The default run budget went from 69 to 75 so every case still gets three runs.
- The native `[project]` tests pass: the tool list has not drifted, and every recorded result matches its schema, the new ones included.
- I re-recorded the full script into a scratch file; the 23 existing points matched apart from ids, timestamps and temporary paths. They are unchanged byte for byte in `requests.json`; the diff only adds the two new points.

The test runner only looks at the first tool call in each model response. In one PETG run, the made-up-purpose `intent_update` came in the same response as a read and was never judged. I left the runner alone and created a follow-up task to fix it, since the change affects every case.

**Your call:** whether to build a one-object fixture and rerun `print-this-no-purpose`. That would be another live run, so I haven't done it. The prompt is unchanged, and the README lists both cases with their results.

The report for an engineer is untracked in the worktree root: [print-setup-cases-report.md](print-setup-cases-report.md).
